facts.F1: Story 6601: Linux standalone builds no longer break when GitHub retires a runner image. The AppImage is built on a GitHub-hosted Ubuntu image with WebKitGTK pinned to that image's package version; when ubuntu-latest moved to 26.04 the pins vanished and the release was blocked; the quick fix pins runs-on: ubuntu-24.04, which breaks again when GitHub retires 24.04. Building on a newer image raises the glibc the AppImage needs and stops it starting on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS and Debian 13. Goal: the Linux build no longer depends on which runner images GitHub offers; the minimum glibc and distribution is a written decision changed on purpose. Acceptance: (1) the Linux standalone builds without naming a GitHub runner image that will be retired, or there is a documented, alarmed path for when it is; (2) the minimum glibc and distribution is written down and CI fails if a build exceeds it; (3) the AppImage still starts on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS.
facts.F10: Paradigm is procedural: GitHub Actions YAML, bash scripts and a pinned container image. No C# or TypeScript production change; mutation testing does not apply. There is no smell catalogue for procedural; the general classes applied are duplicated knowledge (one floor value, one reader), mixed concerns (the check reads facts, the workflow decides when it runs) and hidden coupling (the floor and the container image release must agree, so both are written next to each other and in one ADR).

facts.F162: WebKitGTK pins are dropped: the six exact =2.44.0-2 pins go, so the build takes the current Ubuntu 24.04 versions (release, updates and security) and keeps getting security fixes. The pins were added in March 2026 with no recorded reason and the Tauri code has no WebKit workaround. The floor still comes from the 24.04 base, whose archive keeps glibc 2.39. The build prints the installed libwebkit2gtk-4.1 version into the job log. User-visible risk: a newer WebKitGTK can change rendering, for example the DMABUF renderer showing a blank window on some GPUs; the floor check cannot see it, so the maintainer starts the AppImage of the first build once on a desktop before the release.
facts.F163: Rejected: keep runs-on ubuntu-24.04 (postpones the failure); prebuilt builder image on GHCR like the signing runner image (adds an image pipeline and a registry dependency for a few minutes saved per release; can replace the install step later without touching the floor); keep the exact WebKitGTK pins (no recorded reason, no WebKit workaround, no security updates); scheduled canary on the newest runner (the container removes the dependency the canary would watch, and a vanished ubuntu-latest label fails every job loudly at job start); raising the floor to 26.04 (drops Ubuntu 24.04 users, out of scope); a pull request workflow for the oracles (files change rarely, main runs the floor check).
facts.F164: Test substrate: oracles are bash plus Docker in the style of tools/codesign/tests, summary line observed=N assertions_failed=M setup_failed=K, WHAT/WHY/HOW per failure, no set -e aborts. They need Docker and network. They are not in the default CI suite and no pull request workflow runs them: the files change rarely, and the main build runs the floor check for real. The maintainer runs them locally when these files change. No infrastructure derogation requested.
facts.F165: Floor check carrier: bash script tools/linux-appimage/check-glibc-floor.sh DIR [FLOOR]. It walks DIR with find -type f (symlinks are not followed, so a linked library is read once under its real path), keeps files with the ELF magic 7f454c46, reads the GLIBC_x.y versions each needs from readelf -V (version-needs section, GLIBC_PRIVATE ignored), and compares dotted versions numerically (sort -V semantics, never lexical). Outcomes: exit 0 pass; exit 1 over the floor, one WHAT/WHY/HOW block per offending file naming the path and the highest GLIBC version it needs; exit 2 indeterminate when the directory is missing, readelf is missing, zero ELF files were scanned, or an ELF lists libc.so.6 as needed (readelf -d) and zero GLIBC versions were parsed from it, so a format change cannot read as needs nothing. Summary line scanned=N highest=GLIBC_x.y over_floor=M. readelf comes from binutils and file(1) is not used for the ELF test.
facts.F166: Container constraints: no FUSE, so the Tauri build step sets APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN=1 for linuxdeploy; the libssl rejection step extracts with --appimage-extract and needs no FUSE. The container runs as root, so sudo is dropped. The setup-dotnet step is removed: no later step runs dotnet (the backend arrives as a downloaded artifact, the frontend build is tsc and vite, Tauri is Rust) and the bare image has no ICU library for it. A bare ubuntu image lacks what the GitHub runner image preinstalls, so a first step before checkout installs ca-certificates, curl, wget, git, jq, binutils, build-essential, pkg-config, libssl-dev, libxdo-dev, xz-utils and xdg-utils (git is needed by checkout with fetch-depth 0; curl and ca-certificates by the Rust toolchain action; node comes from setup-node and pnpm from pnpm/action-setup, both JavaScript actions that run in the container). The WebKitGTK dev packages are installed without version pins. The crafter completes the list; the oracle installs exactly what the workflow lists in a fresh digest-pinned container. Not provable locally: the first real Tauri bundling (linuxdeploy and appimagetool download and run in extract-and-run mode, squashfs comes inside appimagetool). That risk is accepted; the rollback is to revert the S2 commit.
facts.F167: Loader check carrier: tools/linux-appimage/check-loads-on.sh IMAGE APPIMAGE extracts the AppImage on the host (APPIMAGE --appimage-extract needs no FUSE) and, in a container of IMAGE, installs the distribution runtime packages libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0 libgtk-3-0t64 librsvg2-2 libayatana-appindicator3-1 (the crafter confirms the names in both images; the oracle shows a wrong one), runs ldd with the AppImage lib directory on LD_LIBRARY_PATH over every ELF in it, and fails on any line saying not found or version GLIBC_ not found. Exit 0 pass, 1 unresolved, 2 indeterminate (no ELF, no AppImage, docker or package install failed). Proof: bundled binaries resolve their libraries and glibc symbols on that distribution. Not proof: the window opens, the backend serves. The workflow gets a second job verify-appimage-loads: needs package-linux-standalone, runs-on ubuntu-latest, checks out the repository for the script, downloads the artifact Lighthouse-linux-standalone-<version> and runs for a matrix of ubuntu:24.04@sha256 and debian:13@sha256 (digests resolved by the crafter): bash tools/linux-appimage/check-loads-on.sh "$IMAGE" ./appimage/Lighthouse-standalone.AppImage. The S2 oracle runs the same script with the same digests it reads from the workflow matrix and the AppImage from the APPIMAGE environment variable. The first main run must show that a failed loader job fails the ci.yml caller and blocks the release job.

The rule in renovate.json that froze the runner image for this workflow is removed and replaced by this rule: {"description": "The Linux AppImage build container is pinned to Ubuntu 24.04 because its glibc is the written floor. Digest updates stay on; a new Ubuntu release changes the floor and needs an ADR.", "matchManagers": ["github-actions"], "matchFileNames": [".github/workflows/ci_package-linux-standalone.yml"], "matchDepNames": ["ubuntu"], "matchUpdateTypes": ["major", "minor"], "enabled": false}. Unverified: whether the github-actions manager reads jobs.*.container images and treats 24.04 to 26.04 as major or minor; if it does not, the first Renovate pull request shows it and the Ubuntu release then stays a human decision. Every other rule is unchanged.
